split_question: Should the Government put more money into the courts so landlord possession cases are heard faster?
angles: Pay for more court staff and judges, funded by taxpayers
Fast-track the clear-cut cases and keep the courts for the hard ones
Help tenants and landlords settle earlier, before a case reaches court
facts_for_writers: Landlord possession claims in England rose 21% to 28,249 in July to September 2026, and accelerated claims rose 68% to a record 12,156 (s1).
Completed landlord repossessions fell 10% to 6,886 in the same quarter (s1, s2).

The median time from claim to landlord possession was 25.9 weeks, down from 27.4 weeks a year earlier; Landlord Today says this may reflect delays to other claims and a rush to evict before the Act took effect (s2).
Section 21 no-fault evictions were abolished in England on 1 May 2026, and landlords with valid older notices generally had until 31 July to start proceedings (s1).
Law Society president Brett Dixon said: "The courts are not appropriately resourced for what was an expected increase" (s2).
